related_questions.question: How long can an executive order stay in effect?

text_blocks.snippet: Executive orders remain in effect until they are revoked by a subsequent president, modified, or declared unlawful by a court. They can also expire if the order itself specifies an end date. Essentially, while they can be powerful tools for a president, their longevity is not guaranteed and can be reversed by future administrations or the courts.

list.title: Revocation:
list.snippet: The most common way an executive order is terminated is when a new president issues an order to revoke or modify it.

list.title: Expiration:
list.snippet: Some executive orders have a specific expiration date built into them, after which they automatically become void.

list.title: Judicial Review:
list.snippet: Courts can also strike down executive orders if they are deemed unconstitutional or exceed the president's authority.

list.title: Congressional Action:
list.snippet: Congress can also invalidate an executive order by passing legislation that contradicts it, though this can be overridden by a presidential veto.
